subject: Social Media
title: Biased Training Data
description: A micro-lesson that makes Biased Training Data usable.

hook.text: An image algorithm labeled Black people as gorillas. Google's fix? Remove the gorilla label entirely.

buildup.text: Algorithms learn from historical data. If that data contains racism, the algorithm reproduces it.

discovery.text: Subtle biases compound: who clicks, who gets shown, who engages. Each layer deepens the skew.

twist.text: Removing race from data creates 'fairness through blindness'—which just ignores real inequities.

climax.text: Researchers now audit algorithms like accountants examine books. Algorithmic accountability is born.

punchline.text: The code isn't biased. The data it ate was.

quiz.question: Why does removing race from training data not fix algorithmic bias?
